definition: Fitness approximation aims to approximate the objective or fitness functions in evolutionary optimization by building up machine learning models based on data collected from numerical simulations or physical experiments.
details: The machine learning models for fitness approximation are also known as meta-models or surrogates, and evolutionary optimization based on approximated fitness evaluations are also known as surrogate-assisted evolutionary approximation. Fitness approximation in evolutionary optimization can be seen as a sub-area of data-driven evolutionary optimization.

explainer.lead: Fitness approximation replaces some expensive fitness calculations in evolutionary optimization with predictions from a learned model. This lets the search use data from numerical simulations or physical experiments instead of directly evaluating every candidate.

tiers.eli5: Imagine testing lots of paper airplane designs, but each test takes a long time. After testing a few, you could learn to make a good guess about the others and use those guesses to guide your search. Fitness approximation works in a similar way.
tiers.practitioner: Train a machine-learning surrogate, or meta-model, on results collected from simulations or experiments, then use its predictions for fitness evaluations in an evolutionary search. The predictions are approximate, so model errors can misguide optimization; newly collected evaluation data can be added to improve the surrogate.
tiers.paperLevel: Given data D = {(x_i, f(x_i))} obtained from numerical simulations or physical experiments, learn a surrogate f_hat(x) that approximates the objective or fitness function f(x). Evolutionary optimization then uses f_hat(x) for approximated fitness evaluations, an approach also called surrogate-assisted evolutionary approximation and regarded as a sub-area of data-driven evolutionary optimization.

explainer.example: Suppose each candidate design requires a lengthy numerical simulation to obtain its fitness. Simulate an initial group of designs, train a surrogate on their results, and let the evolutionary algorithm use the surrogate's predicted fitness values to compare new designs; subsequent simulation results can be added to the training data.

usedIn.name: Data-driven evolutionary optimization
usedIn.detail: Fitness approximation forms a sub-area of this broader approach.

explainer.intuition: Directly measuring every candidate's fitness can require a numerical simulation or physical experiment. A surrogate learns from evaluations already collected and supplies approximate fitness values to guide the evolutionary search.
howItWorks: Evaluate an initial set of candidate solutions using simulations or physical experiments.
Collect the candidates and their measured fitness values as training data.
Train a machine-learning model, called a meta-model or surrogate, on that data.
Use the surrogate's predictions as approximate fitness evaluations during evolutionary optimization.
Use further collected evaluations to extend the data and improve the approximation.
explainer.whyItMatters: It allows evolutionary optimization to proceed using approximate evaluations when direct simulations or experiments are costly or limited. It also connects evolutionary search with machine-learning models built from collected data.
misconceptions: A surrogate does not produce the true fitness function; it supplies an approximation learned from data.
Fitness approximation is not a separate name for evolutionary optimization itself, but a way of supporting its fitness evaluations.
The surrogate does not eliminate the need for simulations or experiments, because their results provide its training data.
